reference: Hand-built cause & effect matrices covering the five spec presets (P1-P5), a clean baseline and one trigger plus one near-miss for each of the 51 review rules CAU-R-001..091 (data validity, opposite-command and trip-versus-permissive conflicts, declared and derived exclusivity with the interval boundary rule and the M_i + M_j > N rule, coverage, safe state, latch and reset, voting independence by device key and by io controller/card/channel, energise/de-energise convention, io fail-state normalisation, bypass provisions, response-time budget, control_functions interlock resolution, analysis method switch at n = 16), scenario sequences for the channel/cause evaluation and the latch/reset acceptance predicate, display-to-SI conversion, matrix-id slug derivation, package item fields, ignored package sections, the mulberry32 check values and two seeded random matrices. Ten further cases (ids prefixed adj-) cover the points spec revision 2026-09-22.2 settled and the ungraded claims the second adjudication pass found. The first four: the spec 3.4 de_energised_state enum, an exclusive pair reached by both the declared and the derived route, the CAU-R-012 target order when the permissive cause is listed first, and the reset refusal reason when two conjuncts of the spec 4.3 predicate fail at once. Expected values were written by hand from SPEC-causeeffect.md rev 2026-09-22.2 and asserted against an own stdlib engine (causeeffect-ref.py); combination counts come from brute force over every subset evaluating the cells directly (spec 4.2), cross-checked against the pairwise count; sampled counts come from an own 32-bit port of mulberry32. Standards clauses are cited as the spec quotes them (IEC 61511-1:2016 10.3.2, 11.8.4, 11.8.5; IEC 61511-1:2003 3.2.45, 11.2.7, 11.6.2, 11.8.3; API RP 14C 7th ed. 4.3.3); the corpus author did not re-read the standard texts, so every rule reference here rests on the spec's formulas. spec 13 names the scenario output 'reset_result' (one result with a reason code) while a case may press reset several times; the corpus grades 'reset_results' as a list in press order, one [result, reason] per press, and adj-reset-reason-precedence is the case that needs the list.

spec 13 writes conflict_pairs as {i, j, effect, kind} and exclusive_pairs as {i, j, source}; the corpus encodes each as a positional array ([i, j, effect, kind], [i, j, source]) so that set equality is a plain comparison of sorted lists. The grader must read the positions, not field names.

Resolved by adjudication 2026-09-23 and moved into SPEC-causeeffect.md rev 2026-09-22.2: safe_state none is legal on any effect class (CAU-R-008 does not fire; r036-safe-state-none corrected); device key 3.8 is explicit and graded; the response-time comparison is exact binary64; AC-3 is scoped to conflict findings; conflict_pairs kind is opposing | trip_vs_permissive; CAU-R-012 uses causes[] order; CAU-R-030 fires beside CAU-R-009 on a wrong-class override; a declared-and-derived pair carries source declared and still raises CAU-R-017; the reset refusal reason is the first failing conjunct (not_latched, mode, location, cause_active).

Spec 3.3.1 states a display -> SI -> display round trip to relative 1e-12, and spec 13 offers one direction only (setpoint_si from a display value).
